CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left hand and wrist numbness, tingling, and pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports several months of left hand and wrist pain and numbness. Symptoms are predominantly nocturnal, with patient awakening with hand asleep and requiring manual stimulation to restore sensation. Numbness affects all fingers but is more prominent in thumb and index finger, with occasional involvement of fifth finger. Associated weakness with difficulty grasping objects due to altered sensation. No clear precipitating event identified. Occupational history significant for heavy landscaping labor with repetitive movements including raking and digging performed daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies rheumatoid arthritis.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works as landscaper performing yard work and maintenance, including flower beds. Work involves heavy repetitive labor (raking, digging) performed daily. Alcohol use: one to two beers on Friday and Saturday weekends.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm.
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation.
Musculoskeletal - Upper extremities: Reduced grip strength on left compared to right. Sensation intact to touch with subjective alteration, more pronounced on thumb side. Bilateral positive Tinel's sign.

RESULTS
EMG ordered to measure electrical impulses in fingers.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome.

1. Activity modification: Reduce repetitive wrist motions by delegating heavy landscaping work to other employees for several weeks.
2. Wrist splint.
3. Ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours.
4. EMG study.
5. Follow-up office visit in 2 weeks.
6. Reassess at follow-up and consider additional diagnostic testing or surgical intervention (nerve release) if inadequate response to conservative management.
